one_liner: DealCloud (Intapp) CRM for private capital has a broad REST API using bearer tokens and a user-generated API key, but it needs a licensed customer site. Its vendor-hosted MCP needs a Celeste license, and it is read-only unless an admin enables write tools.
auth_notes: The user-generated API key is documented on the API Keys page. Requests carry a Bearer token, and the release notes refer to OAuth token generation documented on the token page. That token page was not fetched, so the client-credentials details are unverified. User proxying via the AS-USER header lets an integration act for a principal user. No authorization-code flow for third-party apps is evidenced.
access_notes: The API key is generated in a user's profile inside a customer DealCloud site, and an admin must enable the API capability for the user's group. G2 reports no free plan or trial and says buyers must engage sales for custom enterprise quotes. No public developer sandbox is evidenced.
blocker_notes: There is no self-serve path. A developer needs a licensed DealCloud site with the API capability enabled by an admin or CSM. Each customer site has its own tenant URL and credentials, so toolkit use means per-customer setup. MCP additionally requires the Celeste license.

evidence.quote: Treat your API key like a password: do not share it or expose it in public code repositories.
